note_claims.claim: Increased exertional breathlessness and palpitations for 3 weeks, on a background of atrial fibrillation diagnosed 18 months ago.
Patient is breathless on stairs and experiences palpitations.
Patient has no chest pain.
Patient experiences occasional postural light-headedness but no syncope.
Patient has mild evening ankle swelling.
Patient had a single episode of fresh red rectal bleeding three years ago, which was not previously reported; there has been no recurrence, no melaena, no change in bowel habit, and no weight loss.
Patient is prescribed Apixaban 2.5 mg once daily.
Patient is prescribed Bisoprolol 2.5 mg once daily.
Patient is prescribed Levothyroxine 75 micrograms once daily.
Patient has codeine intolerance (nausea).
Pulse is irregularly irregular at about 104 beats per minute.
Blood pressure is 128/76.
Heart sounds are irregular, and no murmur is heard.
There are fine bibasal crackles.
There is mild bilateral ankle oedema.
Patient's weight is 58 kg.
ECG shows atrial fibrillation with a ventricular rate of approximately 105.
Creatinine is 140, and thyroid function is normal.
Diagnosis is atrial fibrillation with suboptimal rate control, likely contributing to breathlessness, and possible early heart failure.
Reduced renal function is noted (creatinine 140).
Apixaban 2.5 mg twice daily is appropriate given the patient's weight and kidney function.
Continue bisoprolol 2.5 mg once daily.
An echocardiogram is planned within the next six weeks to assess heart pumping function.
Apixaban dose of 2.5 mg twice daily should be continued and not stopped.
A letter will be sent to the GP to arrange a blood count (FBC), FIT test, stool test, and consider a referral to the bowel team.
Attend A&E if there is further significant bleeding, black stools, or feeling faint.
Call 999 if breathing worsens significantly, especially lying flat, or if chest pain occurs.
The patient is scheduled for a clinic review in three months after the echocardiogram.

transcript_facts.fact: Clinician is Dr Sandhu, a cardiology registrar.
Patient's daughter's name is Rosalind.
Patient was diagnosed with atrial fibrillation about eighteen months ago.
Patient has been more puffed out lately, going up the stairs.
Patient can feel their heart fluttering.
Symptoms (breathlessness/palpitations) have been present for three weeks, perhaps a little more.
Clinician asks about chest pain.
Patient reports no chest pain.
Clinician asks about dizziness or blackouts.
Patient experiences light-headedness once or twice when standing up quickly, but has not fainted.
Clinician asks if ankles swell.
Patient reports a little ankle swelling by the evening.
Clinician asks if patient can lie flat at night.
Patient can lie flat at night on one pillow, same as always.
Clinician mentions the patient is on a blood thinner, apixaban.
Patient states they take apixaban once a day in the morning.
Relative corrects the frequency: the patient takes apixaban twice a day (morning and night) and fills the dosette box every Sunday.
Patient confirms the correction: 'Yes, she does the box. Twice then.'
Clinician asks about the dose: 'Five milligrams each time?'
Relative confirms the dose: 'Yes, five milligrams.'
Clinician asks about bleeding problems (nosebleeds, bruising, blood in water or stools).
Patient reports fresh red blood when they went to the toilet three weeks ago.
Relative states the patient never told them about the bleeding.
Clinician asks if the bleeding has happened again since, or if there are any black stools.
Patient reports no further bleeding, just the once.
Clinician asks about change in bowel habit or weight loss.
Patient reports no change in bowel habit or weight loss.
Clinician asks what else the patient takes.
Patient takes bisoprolol 2.5 milligrams and levothyroxine 75 micrograms.
Clinician asks about allergies.
Patient states codeine makes them sick.
Clinician notes intolerance to codeine.
Examination findings: Pulse is irregularly irregular at about 104 a minute.
Examination findings: Blood pressure is 128 over 76.
Examination findings: Heart sounds are irregular, and no murmur is heard.
Examination findings: Chest has a few crackles right at the bases on both sides.
Examination findings: There is mild swelling around both ankles.
Examination findings: Patient's weight is 58 kilos.
Clinician reports bloods from last week: kidney function is reduced with a creatinine of 140, and thyroid level is normal.
Clinician reports ECG findings: atrial fibrillation with a rate of about 105.
Clinician interprets findings: Heart rate is still a bit fast, likely why the patient is more breathless.
Clinician plans to increase the bisoprolol dose from two and a half to five milligrams once a day.
Clinician plans an echocardiogram within the next six weeks to check heart pumping function.
Clinician confirms the apixaban dose of two and a half milligrams twice a day is correct due to weight and kidney function, and plans to keep it the same.
Clinician plans to ask the GP to do a blood count (FBC), FIT test, and stool test, and consider a referral to the bowel team.
Clinician advises against stopping the blood thinner (apixaban) because it would put the patient at risk of a stroke.
Safety-netting advice: Attend A&E if there is further significant bleeding, black stools, or feeling faint.
Safety-netting advice: Call 999 if breathing gets much worse, especially lying flat, or if chest pain occurs.
Follow-up plan: The patient is scheduled to return in three months after the echo.

findings.rationale: The note incorrectly records the Apixaban frequency as once daily, when the transcript confirms it is twice daily (morning and night), which is a critical dosing error for an anticoagulant.
